ov: Mammals covered in large, protective keratin scales, also called scaly anteaters, found in Asia and sub-Saharan Africa. They are nocturnal and solitary, sleep in hollow trees or burrows, and eat mainly ants and termites. Poached for meat and scales, they are the most trafficked mammals in the world.

why.et: Pangolins are poached for their meat and for their scales, which are used in traditional medicine.
why.ac: Nocturnal, feeding mainly on ants and termites.

df: Mainly ants and termites, caught with a long tongue.

cf.tip: Pangolins are sometimes called scaly anteaters, but true anteaters have fur and live in the Americas.

fx: Three species are critically endangered, and all eight assessed species are in a threatened category.
